{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZVsF1g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhC9PNs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 33, "title": "Honor 8237 controller-disable command bit during FDC DMA service", "body": "## Problem

Guest software cannot disable DMA while programming the controller. At baseline `131086f8264026569d25f07c8e83e70ab02860ca`, [`Dma::write`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/131086f8264026569d25f07c8e83e70ab02860ca/src/devices.rs#L239) ignores command-port `0011h` writes. [`Bus::finish_fdc`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/131086f8264026569d25f07c8e83e70ab02860ca/src/bus.rs#L705) checks channel masking but cannot check controller disable. Consequently, an unmasked READ/WRITE DATA command can transfer bytes despite software disabling the controller.

## Expected outcome

Implement the command register's controller-disable bit on both VM and Ap profiles, including its reset contract and interaction with the existing FDC DMA consumer.

Hardware semantics:

- PC-98 maps the DMA command register to write port `11h`. See NEC [IEA-751, §2.4, Table 2-10, printed p.15](https://www.renesas.com/ja/document/apn/upd72070-application-note#page=30).
- Command bit 2 is active-high disable: `1` prevents DMA service; `0` permits service subject to channel masking. Command writes must not reset address/count programming, modes, masks, TC status or the shared byte pointer. Reset and master clear clear the command register. Reading the shared command/status address reads status, not command readback. See Intel [8237A register descriptions, Figure 6 and programming guidance, printed pp.7–11](https://read.seas.harvard.edu/~kohler/class/04f-aos/ref/hardware/8237A.pdf#page=7).
- An FDC data request left unserviced can terminate with abnormal ST0 and ST1 overrun bit 4. See NEC [µPD765A/B, Table 3, PDF p.10](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/UPD765_Datasheet_OCRed.pdf#page=10).

For this repository's existing atomic FDC backend, sample DMA eligibility at the scheduled service boundary. If disabled throughout that boundary, use the existing masked-channel no-service result path: no payload transfer, followed by an overrun result and completion IRQ. This is a bounded scheduling approximation, not a claim about physical timeout duration, DRQ/DACK waveforms or magnetic-media effects. Clearing disable afterward allows a newly issued command to use retained programming; it must not replay a command already completed with an error.

Scope is command-bit-2 behavior, reset, and this existing DMA consumer. Other command bits remain explicitly unsupported. Do not add arbitration, per-byte FDC scheduling or unrelated controller features.

## Context and reproduction

Read-only evaluation confirmed the baseline and inspected the relevant source, tests, previous diff and validation report. No builds, tests or fixture preparation were executed by the evaluator.

Issue #31 / PR #32 added selective master-clear retention. The Coordinator reports eight focused DMA tests, 108 native integration tests and 48 production-Wasm browser tests passing, including baseline-negative checks. These are reported results, not evaluator execution; see [the recorded validation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/131086f8264026569d25f07c8e83e70ab02860ca/docs/validation.md#issue-31-dma-master-clear-retention). That improvement does not implement command controls. No open Issue is listed in the supplied context.

Reproduce with an original patterned floppy image, following the raw-port setup in [`tests/dma.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/131086f8264026569d25f07c8e83e70ab02860ca/tests/dma.rs#L340):

1. Enable the FDC motor/DMA interface, program channel 2's address/count/mode and unmask it.
2. Write `04h` to DMA command port `11h`.
3. Issue a valid raw READ DATA or WRITE DATA command and advance the existing device scheduler through completion.
4. The source currently permits a successful transfer. Expected behavior is no DMA payload service and the bounded overrun completion described above.
5. Write `00h` to `11h`, then issue a fresh command without rewriting DMA programming; service should succeed if the channel remains unmasked.

DMA and integration remain **partial**. All other supplied inventory statuses and required scopes remain unchanged, including mandatory protected mode, paging and basic FPU work. Remaining DMA work includes other command controls, software requests, verify transfers, demand/block/single service and arbitration, rotating priority/cascade, external EOP, memory-to-memory transfers, bank-reset fidelity and broader device interactions. This Issue completes only controller-disable behavior; limited probes establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement the specified command state and eligibility check for both profiles. Preserve existing auto-init, terminal-count and master-clear retention behavior. Master clear must also clear the newly modeled command state while retaining its existing mask/reset contract.
- [ ] Add focused native tests covering repeated disable/enable writes, both byte-pointer phases, status reads while disabled, programming address/count while disabled, and reset/master clear. Assert unrelated programming, masks and latched TC are preserved by command writes. Verify retained bases through a subsequent auto-init transfer.
- [ ] Add raw-port FDC READ and WRITE cases on VM and Ap, covering auto-init on/off. With channel 2 unmasked but the controller disabled, assert unchanged buffer/guards, complete disk image, current DMA registers, masks, TC and transfer counters. For a valid drive-0/head-0 sector-2 command, require exactly `40 10 00 00 00 02 03`, a completion IRQ, seven result bytes and readiness afterward.
- [ ] Cover disabling after command submission but before scheduled service. Re-enabling must not bypass a channel mask. After draining a disabled-command result, clearing disable alone must allow a fresh unmasked command to transfer exact bytes using retained programming, with normal result/IRQ and correct TC or auto-init effects.
- [ ] Extend the original MIT DMA boot probe, or add a separate original source-built probe, with explicit controller-disable PASS/FAIL markers and bounded waits. Record assembly command, license, source/image hashes and execution budget. Execute the same image natively and through production Wasm on VM and Ap at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Preserve all existing auto-init/master-clear assertions and existing game regressions; require no commercial ROM, proprietary firmware or newly acquired game.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the focused native regression and guest probe fail against this baseline because disabled DMA still transfers, and pass with the implementation. Keep baseline comparison isolated from implementation sources.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs and records `cargo test --locked --test dma`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `python3 tools/build_media.py --check`, `python3 tools/build_font.py --check`, and `npm test`, following README fixture preparation and provenance requirements. Preserve existing Rust, hardware, DOS/application/game and browser coverage without weakening assertions or silently skipping fixtures. Report exact commands, outcomes and any environment substitutions.
- [ ] Update the bounded DMA documentation and validation record with supported semantics, scheduling limits, remaining gaps and actual evidence. Resolve blocking review findings before merge.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
